title: Social Selling Index – How to Promote Yourself Effectively on LinkedIn
excerpt: The Social Selling Index (SSI) is LinkedIn's 0–100 score for your personal brand, your network, how you engage with content, and the relationships you build. See how to read it, what your score means, and which steps actually move it.
metaDescription: What is LinkedIn's Social Selling Index (SSI), how do you check it, and how do you read it? The four pillars of the score, why a high number matters, and practical steps that help you raise it.

runs.text: In today's fast-changing digital world, traditional sales methods are slowly giving way to modern communication strategies. As cold calling gets less and less effective and B2B customers research solutions on their own, social selling steps onto the stage. It is not just a buzzword but a powerful methodology that lets you build trust and business relationships where your customers spend their time – on social platforms. As Social Lama, an agency that handles brand communication in social media end to end every day, we know that the foundation of success here is measurability. We are responsible for strategies and engaging content, running ad campaigns on platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok, yet LinkedIn remains the undisputed leader in the B2B sector. To understand how effective your presence on this platform is, you need to get to know a tool called the Social Selling Index (SSI).

In this article you will learn exactly what this score is, how to check it, and – most importantly – how to genuinely improve it so that it translates into real sales results. LinkedIn is not just a digital résumé; it is a space where every LinkedIn user has a shot at becoming an opinion leader in their industry. The key is understanding the mechanics of the algorithm and putting the available tools to good use. Many people decide to subscribe to LinkedIn Premium to unlock extended analytics and broader search options, which directly supports building a professional brand. Still, even the most advanced tools will never replace a well-thought-out strategy and consistency.

The Social Selling Index (SSI) is a parameter that lets you assess how effectively you deliver on the four main pillars of social selling. Understanding what the Social Selling Index is made of lets you pinpoint the areas that need optimization. Clients often ask us whether improving this score is worth the time. The answer is simple: the statistics show that people with a high SSI generate 45% more sales opportunities than those with a low one. If your goal is effective, professional LinkedIn management, you cannot ignore the data the platform serves you. Analyzing these parameters is exactly what lets us at Social Lama build communication strategies that genuinely engage potential customers and create a lasting competitive edge.

To make the most of what today's social media can offer, it pays to look beyond a single platform. An effective online presence takes integrated action on many fronts. If a comprehensive approach interests you, have a look at our article <a0>Social media management</a0>, where we describe in detail how we help companies build their digital image. But back to the point – how do you read an SSI score, and what do you do to climb your industry's rankings?
What exactly is the Social Selling Index (SSI)?

The Social Selling Index (SSI) is a score developed by LinkedIn that measures your progress across the four main components of social selling. It is updated daily and available free to every LinkedIn account holder. The score rates your activity on a scale from 0 to 100 points. As the platform's own research shows, there is a strong correlation between a high SSI and hitting sales targets. Think of it as a "thermometer" for your business presence.
The SSI is built on four main components, each worth up to 25 points:

Before you go all in, you should check your Social Selling Index so you know where you are starting from. All it takes is being logged in to your account and visiting the dedicated LinkedIn Sales Navigator SSI page. Your individual score is set against people in your industry and in your network, which gives you an excellent point of reference.
Pillar 1: Establish your professional brand

The first element of the score focuses on how other users perceive you. To build your personal brand effectively, your professional profile has to be complete and customer-oriented, not just a list of your past achievements. Remember that your profile is your business card – it has to answer the question: "How can I help my potential customer?"
To improve this part of the score, take care of:
A professional profile photo and a well-designed background image.
A headline that contains the keywords that matter in your industry.
An "About" section that tells the story of your customers' successes, not just your own.
Publishing valuable content that backs up your expertise.

When you regularly publish valuable content and keep your profile up to date, LinkedIn's algorithm starts to see you as an active, valuable member of the community. That in turn means a higher position in search results when others look for specialists with your skills. Your professional brand is the foundation that all of social selling rests on.
Pillar 2: Find the right people

In traditional sales we often waste time talking to people with no decision-making power. LinkedIn shortens that path dramatically. The find the right people component rates how effectively you identify potential customers and decision makers. Advanced search filters let you reach precisely the people who might actually be interested in your services.

This is a good moment to mention Sales Navigator, a tool that makes finding leads much easier. It lets you monitor job changes at the companies you care about and follow the activity of key people. For your Social Selling Index score in this category to grow, you should not only search for people's profiles but also visit the profiles of people in your target group and check who has visited yours. That mutual overlap of networks is key to building relationships in business.
Pillar 3: Engage with insights

This is the heart of any social selling program. A profile and a network alone are not enough – you have to be visible. The engage with insights component measures how often you share other people's material, publish your own posts, and interact. LinkedIn promotes users who deliver value.

When you comment on the posts of industry leaders, take part in group discussions, and share data from reports, you build your authority. The algorithm pays attention to whether your content sparks discussion. The more engaging with content becomes part of your daily routine, the higher your SSI score climbs. Just don't do it mechanically. Valuable content educates, inspires, or solves a specific problem for your network. At Social Lama we put enormous emphasis on communication being natural and authentic – only then does it stand a chance of cutting through the noise. Our agency, handling communication end to end, makes sure every publication is part of a bigger strategy, which lets us systematically improve our clients' Social Selling Index.
Pillar 4: Build relationships

The last pillar is the essence of networking. LinkedIn rates how you build and maintain relationships with your network. It is not about the number of connections but their quality. Sending mass invitations with no personalization is the fastest way to undermine your credibility.
To raise your selling index in this area:
Send personalized connection requests.
Connect with people in senior roles (the decision makers).
Keep relationships alive with direct messages in which you don't sell right away but offer help or share an interesting article.
Build trust by being a helpful member of your industry.

Understanding that social selling is a marathon, not a sprint, is key. Building valuable relationships takes time and patience. The SSI score rewards those who are consistent and focused on giving value to other users.
Why is a high SSI so important for your company?

You might think a social score is just a number meant to flatter salespeople's egos. Nothing could be further from the truth. The statistics show that leaders with a high SSI are 51% more likely to hit their sales targets. Why is that? The answer lies in trust. In the era of traditional sales, the salesperson was an intruder. In the social selling model, the salesperson becomes an advisor and an expert.

When you are active on LinkedIn, your personal brand works for you even while you sleep. Potential customers often check your profile before deciding to get in touch. Seeing a high Social Selling Index, regular posts, and confirmed skills, they are far more willing to start a conversation. That sales potential is exactly why more and more companies decide to roll out social selling processes in their sales teams.
How to read your SSI score?
Once you check your current score, you may feel a little lost. What does 60 points mean? And 80?
Below 40: A sign that your account is fairly passive. You probably rarely post and don't make new connections.
40–60: An average score, showing that you know the basics but aren't using LinkedIn's full potential.
60–80: A very good level. You are seen as an expert and you use the platform actively.
Above 80: You belong to the elite (usually the top 1% of your industry). You are a genuine opinion leader and social selling is second nature to you.

Remember that a low score at the start is nothing to be ashamed of. It is a roadmap that shows where you have the most room to grow. If your "find the right people" bar is low, focus on sharpening your target group. If "engage with insights" is lagging – start by commenting on a few posts a day.
Practical steps to improve your Social Selling Index
To raise your Social Selling Index (SSI) score effectively, you don't need an army of people – you need a strategy. Here are a few steps you can put in place right away:
Optimize your personal profile: Make sure every section is filled in. Use the keywords your customers use.
Set a publishing rhythm: You don't have to write every day. Start with 2–3 valuable posts a week. Consistency matters more than volume.
Be interactive: Spend 15 minutes a day reacting to other people's posts. Remember: the "social" in social media means being social.
Build your network deliberately: Don't accept every invitation and don't send them blindly. Look for people who can genuinely benefit from your knowledge or become your business partners.

The technical side matters too. LinkedIn's algorithm rewards making use of LinkedIn data and tools like the Sales Navigator mentioned earlier. But even without paid accounts, by following the rules above you can reach an impressive high score.
Social selling is not just LinkedIn

Although the LinkedIn Social Selling Index is the best-known measure, the philosophy carries over to all social media. Building a brand, delivering value, and forming relationships are universal rules. At Social Lama we know how to connect those dots. We create consistent campaigns that start with educating the customer on LinkedIn and end with engaging ads on Instagram or TikTok. Comprehensiveness is our strength – from strategy, through content creation, to advanced analytics.

Selling online keeps evolving. Today it is not enough to simply "be there." You have to be visible, credible, and helpful. The score developed by LinkedIn is an excellent supporting tool, but the real goal is building a strong brand, resilient to market change, that attracts valuable contacts naturally.
Summary

Reaching the level where you have a high SSI is not just a matter of prestige but a real driver of your company's growth. It is a process that teaches us how to listen to the market and how to answer its needs without being pushy. Remember that there is a human being behind every profile, and social selling is nothing more than a modern form of building trust.

If you feel you need support in this process, or want your company to show up in social media with fresh energy, remember the experts. We at Social Lama will gladly help you go from random actions to a thought-through strategy that delivers results.
FAQ – Frequently asked questions
Does a high SSI score guarantee me sales?

The score itself is only an indicator of your activity and visibility. Although a high Social Selling Index statistically raises your chances of success, the final sale depends on the quality of your product, your negotiation skills, and how well you can move a relationship from online to direct business contact.
How often should I check my current SSI score?

We recommend checking the score once a week. Daily monitoring can be frustrating, because changes often come from day-to-day swings in the activity of your network. A weekly interval makes it easier to spot the trends that come from your own actions, such as regular publishing or actively searching for new leads.
Do I need a paid account (e.g. Sales Navigator) to have a high SSI?

It isn't necessary, although it does help in the "Find the right people" category. LinkedIn favors users of its paid tools with a small scoring "bonus," but most of the points come from organic activity: optimizing your profile, publishing valuable content, and real interactions with other users. Every personal profile has a shot at a score above 75–80 points with no extra fees.
